name: Notional Equity Drawdown Ratchet
note: The Turtle size ratchet, isolated. Position size is taken off a NOTIONAL equity of actual_equity * (1-cut)^k with k = floor(current drawdown / step), restored only on a new all-time equity high, so 30% down leaves about half size on 70% of the capital. The base signal is deliberately plain - a 20-bar Donchian break with a 2 ATR(20) stop and flat on the opposite signal - so the only variable is the size rule. Sizing is applied by setting ctx.p.shares, the one execution lever a family may touch; the ratchet never blocks a trade, it only shrinks one. Size is the Turtle unit itself - risk_frac of the notional equity divided by the 2 ATR(20) stop - capped at max_lev times notional so a low-ATR symbol cannot buy an unbounded position.
source: Original Turtle Trading Rules, 'Adjusting Trading Size' - 'when the account dropped 10%, all unit sizes were cut by 20%, with further reductions at every additional 10% drawdown'. https://oxfordstrat.com/coasdfASD32/uploads/2016/01/turtle-rules.pdf
code:
def family_init(ctx):
    """Turtle drawdown ratchet. The signal is a plain 20-bar Donchian break so
    that the only thing being studied is the SIZE rule sitting on top of it:
    every 10% of drawdown from the equity peak cuts the notional the position
    is sized off by 20%, and only a new all-time high restores it.
    """
    bars = ctx.bars
    n = len(bars)
    hi = [float(b["h"]) for b in bars]
    lo = [float(b["l"]) for b in bars]
    cl = [float(b["c"]) for b in bars]

    w = max(2, int(ctx.p.don))
    sig = [0] * n
    for i in range(w, n):
        ph = max(hi[i - w:i])              # prior w bars, current bar excluded
        pl = min(lo[i - w:i])
        if cl[i] > ph:
            sig[i] = 1
        elif cl[i] < pl:
            sig[i] = -1

    ctx.sig = ctx.series(sig, "donchian_break")
    ctx._peak = float(ctx.p.start_cap)
    ctx._k = 0


def _resize(ctx, i):
    """notional_equity = actual_equity * (1 - cut)^k, k = floor(dd / step).

    Sizing is the one execution lever a family is allowed to touch, and this
    idea IS a sizing rule, so it is applied by setting ctx.p.shares before the
    shared harness reads it. It never blocks a trade, it only shrinks one.
    """
    eq = float(ctx.p.start_cap) + ctx.equity
    if eq > ctx._peak:
        ctx._peak = eq                     # new all-time high resets the ladder
        ctx._k = 0
    step = float(ctx.p.dd_step)
    if ctx._peak > 0 and step > 0:
        dd = (ctx._peak - eq) / ctx._peak
        ctx._k = int(dd / step) if dd > 0 else 0
    mult = (1.0 - float(ctx.p.cut)) ** ctx._k
    fl = float(ctx.p.mult_floor)
    if mult < fl:
        mult = fl
    notional = eq * mult
    a = ctx.a[i]
    if a is None or a <= 0 or notional <= 0:
        ctx.p.shares = 1
        return
    risk = float(ctx.p.risk_frac) * notional
    n = int(risk / (float(ctx.p.st_atr) * a))
    if n < 1:
        n = 1
    cap = int(ctx.p.max_shares)
    px = ctx.c[i]
    if px > 0:
        lev = int(float(ctx.p.max_lev) * notional / px)
        if lev < cap:
            cap = lev
    if n > cap:
        n = cap
    if n < 1:
        n = 1
    ctx.p.shares = n


def signal(ctx, i):
    _resize(ctx, i)
    return ctx.sig[i]
